pages.text: One cold morning, Dot looked out the window. Snow covered everything! Dot wanted to build a snow friend. Dot pulled on a warm hat and ran outside.
Dot rolled a big snowball and a small one. Dot stacked them up. Then a puppy ran by and knocked the top off!
Dot laughed. Dot and the puppy rolled a new top together. Now the snow friend was done, and Dot had a new friend.

find.prompt: Tap the page where the middle starts.

pages.text: Pip was a small frog in a quiet pond. Every night, Pip looked up at the twinkly stars. Pip loved them.
Pip wanted to see the stars up close. How many were there? Nobody in the pond knew. Pip had to find out!
Pip climbed the tallest tree. The stars were still far away. A kind owl offered a ride. Pip felt a bit scared, but brave too.
Up they flew, past the clouds. The stars sparkled all around. Pip counted and counted, and smiled all night long.

find.sentence: Pip wanted to see the stars up close.

pages.text: Mo the bear was sick in bed all week. Tam the rabbit felt sad for Mo. Tam wanted to cheer Mo up, so Tam baked a carrot cake.
Tam carried the cake to the river. But the little bridge had washed away! Tam felt so worried. How could a rabbit get across?
Tam tried hopping on the stones, but the cake wobbled. Then a big turtle swam up. The turtle let Tam ride across, cake and all!
Mo opened the door and grinned a big bear grin. Tam felt warm and proud inside. They shared the cake with the turtle.

find.prompt: Tap where something gets in Tam's way.
find.sentence: But the little bridge had washed away!

pages.text: Kit the fox won a red balloon at the fair. Kit tied the string to one paw and skipped home, humming.
Then a gust of wind tugged the string loose. The balloon floated up into a tall tree!
Kit climbed up to grab it, but the wind blew harder. Whoosh! The balloon sailed over the hill, toward the dark clouds. Kit wanted to cry.
Kit ran up the hill, faster and faster. Kit jumped high and caught the string! Kit hugged the balloon and held on tight all the way home.

pages.text: Ollie the bear woke up with a rumbly tummy. Grrrumble! Ollie wanted honey, sweet and sticky.
But the honey pot was empty! Ollie sniffed the air. Something smelled sweet, like flowers in the sun.
Ollie followed the smell to a tall tree. Bzzz! The bees buzzed loud and grumpy. Ollie felt a little scared.
Ollie picked the bees a bunch of flowers. The bees shared a drip of warm, golden honey. It tasted like sunshine!

find.prompt: Tap the sentence that tells what the smell is like.
find.sentence: Something smelled sweet, like flowers in the sun.

pages.text: Pim the rabbit packed a picnic basket. "Let's eat by the pond!" Pim said. Fig the fox clapped. "Yes! I'll bring the cake."
But at the pond, dark clouds rolled in. Plip, plop! "Oh no," Fig said. "Our picnic is all soggy."
Pim spotted a big tree with thick leaves. "Quick, under here!" Pim shouted. The leaves kept them dry.
They ate cake and listened to the rain. "This is the best picnic ever," Fig said. Pim grinned. "Next time, let's ask for rain!"
Juno the cat loved to sing. Juno wanted to sing at the school show. On show day, Juno's tummy did flip-flops.
Juno peeked at the crowd. So many faces! Juno's paws shook, and Juno's voice came out as tiny as a squeak.
Then Juno spotted Pip the frog in the front row. Pip waved and gave a big thumbs-up. Juno took a deep breath.
Juno sang loud and clear. Everyone clapped and cheered! Juno's tail swished, and Juno bowed with the biggest grin.

find.prompt: Tap where you can tell how Juno feels.
find.sentence: Juno's paws shook, and Juno's voice came out as tiny as a squeak.

pages.text: Olo was a little owl with a big problem. Olo was scared of the dark! Every night, Olo hid in the nest with a lantern.
Olo's friends flew off to see the moon. Olo wanted to go too. So Olo held the lantern tight and flew out slowly.
Then, puff! The wind blew the lantern out. Olo shivered. But slowly, Olo's big eyes could see. The moon made the leaves shine silver.
Olo flapped up to the friends by the moon. Now Olo loves the dark, and the lantern stays home.

find.sentence: Now Olo loves the dark, and the lantern stays home.
